This component ingeniously spells out the phrase "PROMPTING IS ALL YOU NEED" using a grid of customizable pixels, which then become breakable blocks in a classic arcade experience. To celebrate the 21st Dev anniversary, here's a description of your PromptingIsAllYouNeed component, perfect for sharing!  PromptingIsAllYouNeed: Interactive Pixel-Art Pong Canvas Celebrate the spirit of innovation with PromptingIsAllYouNeed, a unique React component that transforms your browser into an interactive, full-screen Pong-like game. This component ingeniously spells out the phrase "PROMPTING IS ALL YOU NEED" using a grid of customizable pixels, which then become breakable blocks in a classic arcade experience.  What It Is: This component renders a dynamic canvas where a bouncy ball navigates the screen, interacting with four paddles positioned at each edge. The core phrase, "PROMPTING IS ALL YOU NEED," is displayed in a retro pixel-art style. As the ball collides with these pixels, they change color, simulating a "hit" effect, much like breaking blocks in a game of Breakout. The paddles on all four sides automatically track and follow the ball's movement, keeping the action continuous and mesmerizing.  Key Features: Pixel Art Text: The central message "PROMPTING IS ALL YOU NEED" is rendered using custom pixel maps for each letter, offering a distinct retro aesthetic. Interactive Gameplay: A ball continuously bounces around the screen, changing direction upon hitting the canvas edges, the paddles, or the pixel-art letters. Dynamic Paddles: Four automated paddles (top, bottom, left, right) intelligently track the ball's position, ensuring constant interaction and deflections. Breakable Pixels: Each time the ball hits a pixel in the text, its color changes from white to gray, visually indicating a "hit." Responsive Design: The canvas and all game elements (pixel size, ball radius, paddle dimensions, and speeds) dynamically adjust to fit any screen size, ensuring a seamless experience across devices. Configurable Colors: Easily customize the background, ball, paddle, text, and hit-pixel colors directly within the component's constants. Smooth Animations: Utilizes requestAnimationFrame for fluid game loops, providing a smooth and engaging visual experience.

description: This component is ideal for an "About Us" or "Services" section on a company website, particularly for businesses in design, architecture, or related creative fields. It provides a modern, engaging, and informative presentation of the company's capabilities and achievements.  Key Features: Responsive Layout: The component adapts its layout for different screen sizes, arranging content in a single column on small screens and a multi-column grid on larger ones. Parallax Background Elements: Decorative circular elements in the background move and rotate subtly based on scroll position, adding depth and visual interest. "About Us" Header: A clear and concise "About Us" heading is accompanied by a subtitle and an animated underline, effectively introducing the section. Company Introduction: A central paragraph provides a brief overview of the company's mission and values. Service Offerings: Six distinct service items (Interior, Exterior, Design, Decoration, Planning, Execution) are displayed. Each service includes an icon, a title, and a description. Services are strategically placed in left and right columns, flanking a central image. The ServiceItem sub-component features hover animations for icons and titles, along with a "Learn more" link that appears on hover. Central Image with Call to Action: A prominent image (Modern House) serves as a visual anchor. It features a subtle border animation, floating accent elements, and an overlaid "Our Portfolio" button that appears on hover. Animated Statistics (StatCounter): Four key statistics (Projects Completed, Happy Clients, Years Experience, Satisfaction Rate) are displayed with an animated counter format. The StatCounter sub-component uses framer-motion's useSpring and useTransform to animate numerical values as they come into view. Each stat includes an icon, a numerical value with a suffix, and a descriptive label, along with hover effects for the icon and a line underneath. Call to Action (CTA) Section: A clear and inviting call-to-action at the bottom prompts users to "Get Started" and encourages them to transform their space. Framer Motion Integration: The component heavily uses framer-motion for: Orchestrated Entrance Animations: Elements fade in and slide up or across as the section comes into view. Hover Effects: Interactive animations on service items, the central image button, and stat counters. Parallax Scrolling: Dynamic movement of background and accent elements based on scroll. Spring Animations: Smooth counting animation for statistics. Modular Design: The section is composed of reusable sub-components (ServiceItem and StatCounter), promoting organized and reusable code.  The AboutUsSection component presents key information about a company—likely an interior design or architectural firm—through a combination of text, service listings, an engaging image, and animated statistics. It's built with a focus on modern aesthetics and user experience, incorporating subtle animations and parallax effects to create an immersive feel.

name: Text Parallax Content (scroll)
description: TextParallaxContent: Engaging Scroll-Triggered Narratives Unleash a dynamic storytelling experience on your website with TextParallaxContent, a versatile React component designed to blend captivating visuals with compelling narratives. This component creates an immersive scrolling effect where text overlays animate in and out, while a "sticky" image scales and fades, providing a truly engaging user journey.  Features Interactive Parallax Effect: As users scroll, a large background image remains "sticky" in the viewport while subtly scaling down and fading out. Simultaneously, a headline and subheading animate into view, crossfade, and then exit, creating a powerful visual and textual interplay. Modular Content Blocks: The component is designed to be easily repeatable. You can stack multiple TextParallaxContent instances to create a series of distinct narrative sections, each with its own image and text, allowing you to tell a sequential story or highlight different aspects of your product or service. Customizable Content: Each instance accepts imgUrl, subheading, and heading props, along with children for additional customizable content below the main parallax section. This allows for flexible integration of more detailed information, calls to action, or other elements. Smooth Animations: Built with Framer Motion, all animations are fluid and performant, ensuring a seamless and delightful user experience. Responsive Design: The component adapts beautifully to various screen sizes, maintaining its visual impact on both desktop and mobile devices. How it Works TextParallaxContent leverages Framer Motion's powerful useScroll and useTransform hooks to link scroll progress to various CSS properties:  StickyImage: This sub-component uses useTransform to control the scale and opacity of the image based on scroll position, creating the "sticky" and fading effect. OverlayCopy: This sub-component also uses useTransform to animate the y position and opacity of the text overlays, making them slide and fade in and out as they pass through the viewport. useRef: Used to target specific DOM elements for scroll tracking, ensuring precise animation triggers. TextParallaxContent is ideal for "about us" sections, product features, service descriptions, or any part of your site where you want to combine strong imagery with a narrative flow that unfolds as the user scrolls.

name: Elastic Line
description: A wobbly svg line with a spring cursor interaction.  This component is made with a simple svg quadratic curve, with 2+1 points. The start and end points of the curve positioned at the two edges of the parent container, either horizontally or vertically, depending on the isVertical prop. This means, the line will always be centered in the container, and it will always fill up the entire container, so make sure to position your container properly.  The third point of the line is the control point, named Q, which is positioned at the center of the container by default. When the cursor moves close to the line (within grabThreshold), the control point will be controlled by the cursor's position. When the distance between them is greater than the releaseThreshold prop, the control point is animated back to the center of the container, with the help of motion's animate function.  For better readability — the calculation of the control point's position, and the signal it's grabbed — done in a separate hook, called useElasticLineEvents.  To achiave the elastic effect we use a springy transition by default, but feel free to experiment with other type of animations, easings, durations, etc.  The compoment also have an animateInTransition prop, which is used when the line is initially rendered. If you want to skip this, just set the transiton's duration to 0.

name: Vertical Cut Reveal
description: A text component that reveals the text with a cut reveal effect.  First, the text gets split into smaller chunks based on the splitBy prop: 	•	words: Splits into individual words (e.g., "Hello world" → \["Hello", "world"\]) 	•	characters: Splits into individual characters (e.g., "Hi" → \["H", "i"\]) 	•	lines: Splits by newline characters (\\n) 	•	string: Splits by any custom string delimiter Each text piece is wrapped in two <span> elements: 	•	An outer <span> acts as a container, set to position: relative and overflow: hidden. 	•	An inner <span> holds the actual text, initially positioned off-screen using y: 100 (or -100 if reverse is true). When the animation kicks off: 	•	The inner <span> elements smoothly transition from their off-screen position (y: 100) to their final position (y: 0). 	•	This creates a "cutting" or "revealing" effect as each text piece slides into view. You can stagger the animation from different directions (first, last, center, or random) using the staggerFrom prop. A key detail is that the component always keeps word boundaries, even when splitting by characters. Here are two reasons why: 	1.	When dealing with multi-line text, each line starts its own reveal animation. So, if you have text that spans multiple lines, each line animates independently from its own baseline, instead of all elements animating from one point (like the bottom of the entire paragraph). 	2.	In characters mode, characters from the same word stick together in a word container. This stops unwanted line breaks in the middle of words. If a word needs to wrap to the next line, it wraps as a complete unit, keeping some characters from one line and others from the next. This keeps the text flowing and readable while still allowing character-by-character animation within each word.
author: Daniel Petho

description: A component that types out a text, one letter at a time.  As a text, either a string or an array of strings can be passed to the component. The component will automatically split the text into an array of characters, and animate each letter one by one. If you pass an array of strings, the component will animate one text, delete it, then continue animating the next one. The component will loop through the texts if you set the loop prop to true.  The cursor at the end of the text is optional. You can use a character or even a svg node if you like. There is a prop to customize the cursor animation, where you have to define the two motion variants as initial and animate.  Ideally, the component should respect multiple lines. If you experience otherwise, please let me know.:)

name: Underline Animation
description: A component that animates a text underline.  These underline animations work differently from typical CSS underline animations. Instead of animating the CSS text-decoration-line: underline property, they create a separate div element positioned absolutely below the text. This div acts as the underline and its dimensions are calculated relative to the font size:  - The height is controlled by underlineHeightRatio (defaults to 10% of font size) - The padding below text is controlled by underlinePaddingRatio (defaults to 1% of font size)  The three variants work as follows: - Center: The underline grows outward from the center point - Comes In Goes Out: The underline enters from one side, then exits from the other side - Goes Out Comes In: The underline exits from one side, then re-enters from the opposite side

The mirror is a real 3D object standing inside a 360-degree photograph, with true portal rendering (the other world is rendered live through the glass), image-based lighting, a dimension-shift post effect at the crossing, look-around with inertia once you arrive, and procedural sound that stays off until you turn it on. Immersive Visual Effects — A distinctive geometric network background with a futuristic, technology-inspired aesthetic.

Conversion-Focused Layouts — Clear messaging, prominent calls to action, and thoughtfully structured content.

Customizable Design System — Reusable UI components and design tokens for effortless brand customization.

about: Karakeep brings bookmarked links, written notes, and saved images into one application. It provides full-text search and optional automated enrichment to help organize collected material.

name: Umami: Website analytics
description: Explore traffic, referrers, events, and visitor trends in one dashboard.
about: Umami is a web analytics application with traffic summaries, event reporting, and breakdowns by page, referrer, device, and location. Teams can share read-only dashboards and compare date ranges. Its Next.js source supports self-hosting with a PostgreSQL database.

name: Memos: Quick notes
description: Capture short notes and organize a personal knowledge timeline.
about: Memos is a self-hosted application for recording ideas, notes, and everyday information. Its web interface presents entries in a timeline and supports Markdown and attached content. The source provides a practical base for a lightweight note-taking product built around fast capture and retrieval.

name: Linkwarden: Research collections
description: Collect, annotate, and preserve useful pages in shared link collections.
about: Linkwarden is a bookmark and reading application that combines organization with page preservation. It can store page copies and supports reading, annotations, and collaboration around collected material.

name: OpenResume: Resume builder
description: Build a resume with a live PDF preview and adjustable typography.
about: OpenResume provides a structured resume editor with work experience, education, projects, and skills sections. Its preview updates as the content and formatting change. The application also includes a PDF resume parser and runs its editing workflow in the browser.

name: EasyInvoicePDF
description: Create invoices in the browser with a live PDF preview.
about: EasyInvoicePDF provides an invoice editor with configurable document details, templates, and PDF export. The editor updates a document preview as invoice fields change, so users can prepare an invoice and download the resulting PDF from the same workspace.

name: Drawnix: Whiteboard and diagrams
description: A browser whiteboard for mind maps, flowcharts, and freehand sketches.
about: Drawnix combines an open canvas with diagramming tools for organizing ideas visually. Its React application supports mind maps, flowcharts, freehand drawing, and conversion from Mermaid or Markdown. Start here when your product needs a diagram editor or visual planning workspace.

name: JSON Crack: Visual data editor
description: Explore structured data as an interactive graph while editing its source.
about: JSON Crack pairs a structured-data editor with an interactive graph. It supports JSON, YAML, CSV, and XML workflows, formatting and validation, generated schemas and types, and image export. The repository contains the complete Next.js web editor alongside its integrations.

name: Kan: Team kanban boards
description: Organize project work into boards, lists, and cards with labels and shared context.
about: Kan is a project management application built around kanban boards. Cards support labels, comments, activity history, and reusable board templates. Teams can manage board visibility, collaborate in workspaces, and publish selected boards for read-only viewing. The source uses Next.js, React, and PostgreSQL.

name: Lyftr: Workout log
description: Record sets and exercises, follow workouts, and review training history.
about: Lyftr is a workout tracking application with a React web client and a Go backend. It combines exercise records, workout logs, rest timing, and related personal tracking screens.

name: OpenPanel: Product analytics
description: Explore events, visitor journeys, and funnels in a product analytics workspace.
about: OpenPanel is a product and website analytics application with dashboards for understanding usage. It includes event-oriented analysis, funnels, and profile views alongside traffic reporting. Its TypeScript source provides a base for a product analytics service with collection APIs and an interactive web dashboard.

name: Meerkat: Personal relationships
description: Keep contact notes, birthdays, and relationship reminders in one place.
about: Meerkat is a personal relationship manager for keeping context about the people in your life. Its Go and React application organizes contact notes, birthdays, and other dates relevant to staying in touch.

name: Rybbit: Website analytics
description: Explore traffic, pages, referrers, events, and visitor journeys in a web analytics dashboard.
about: Rybbit is a web analytics application with site dashboards, traffic charts, page and referrer reports, and custom event analysis. It includes filters, goals, funnels, and user journey views. Its source combines a Next.js and React client with services for collecting and querying analytics data.

name: EdgeEver: Notes workspace
description: Organize notes in a three-pane library with rich text and Markdown editing.
about: EdgeEver is a notes and knowledge application with a React web frontend. Its three-pane workspace combines structured browsing, editing, and search with import and revision-oriented workflows.

name: Metabase: Business intelligence dashboards
description: Explore database data through visual questions, charts, and shareable dashboards.
about: Metabase is a business intelligence application for querying data and building dashboards. It provides a visual query builder alongside SQL, chart configuration, filters, and dashboard sharing. The open-source core includes a React frontend and can connect to supported databases in a self-hosted deployment.

name: Atomic CRM: Contacts and deal pipelines
description: Manage contacts, companies, sales opportunities, notes, and follow-up tasks in one CRM.
about: Atomic CRM is a customer relationship management application with company and contact records, a kanban deal pipeline, tasks, and activity history. Its React interface includes configurable fields and sales stages. The self-hosted application uses Supabase, and the public demo provides a browser-local sample workspace.

name: BetterShift: Shift calendars
description: Organize work shifts with reusable presets and shared calendars.
about: BetterShift is a Next.js shift management application for individuals and teams. It supports several calendars, reusable shift patterns, shared access, and calendar exports.

name: Rallly: Group scheduling
description: Find a meeting time by collecting availability in a shared poll.
about: Rallly lets an organizer propose dates and times, share a poll, and compare participants' availability. Its interface includes an availability grid, comments, and a final date selection. The Next.js source is useful for a scheduling product with a clear guest-facing flow and collaborative decision making.

name: EmailBuilder.js: Visual email editor
description: Compose product emails with reusable blocks, sample layouts, and responsive previews.
about: EmailBuilder.js includes a complete visual email editor built with React. Start from welcome messages, receipts, reminders, or reports, then adjust content and styles in the inspector. The editor exposes HTML and JSON output and desktop and mobile previews.

name: Marimo
description: Build an interactive data notebook with Python cells, charts and a reactive editor.
about: Marimo brings Python code, Markdown, interactive charts and data inspection into a reactive notebook editor. Notebooks are stored as Python source. The preview runs the official numerical-embedding example in WebAssembly and opens its variables panel; heavier workloads can use a Python server. The application has a React and TypeScript frontend.

name: Icônes
description: Build an icon browsing app with instant search, collections and code exports.
about: Icônes provides a searchable interface for browsing icon collections, choosing symbols and copying their usage. The Vue application includes category filters and local favorites. Its preview demonstrates calendar and camera searches in the Lucide collection. Individual icon collections retain their own licenses.

name: Apache Answer
description: Build a question-and-answer community with searchable topics, tags and voting.
about: Apache Answer provides question pages, accepted answers, tags, search, voting and community reputation. Its React interface and Go backend can serve a team knowledge base or a public support community. The video explores the official public community and tag directory without submitting content. Running your own instance requires a database.

about: OpenPencil is a browser design editor with a layered canvas, reusable components and a properties panel. Its sample file demonstrates cards, gradients and interface elements. The recording selects a layer and switches between its design properties and generated code.

name: CodeImage
description: Build a code screenshot editor with live themes, typography and frame controls.
about: CodeImage turns code snippets into styled visual cards. Its SolidJS interface combines a live preview with theme selection, typography, padding and window controls. The video demonstrates three actual theme changes in the guest editor.

name: Papra
description: Build a document archive with search, tags and a focused file library.
about: Papra provides a searchable home for documents, receipts and personal files. Its SolidJS interface includes tags, saved views and quick search. The video uses the official browser-local demo with bundled sample documents and a real receipt search.

name: Fider: Customer feedback portal
description: Collect feature requests, organize feedback, and discuss product ideas in a public portal.
about: Fider is a feedback portal for feature requests and suggestions. People can browse ideas, follow discussions, and vote on requests, while teams organize feedback with tags and statuses. The application combines a React frontend with a Go backend and can be self-hosted.

name: Hoppscotch: API workspace
description: Compose API requests and inspect responses in a browser workspace.
about: Hoppscotch provides an API client with request parameters, headers, bodies, and response inspection. Requests can be organized into collections, and the application includes HTTP and realtime protocol workspaces. Its web interface is built with Vue and can be used as a base for an API testing product.

name: Immich: Photo and video library
description: Browse, organize, and share a self-hosted photo collection.
about: Immich is a photo and video management application with a web library and mobile clients. It supports browsing a personal collection, organizing albums, and searching media.

name: IT Tools
description: Everyday encoding, conversion, and debugging tools in one web app.
about: IT Tools collects small interactive utilities for developers and technical work. Its Vue interface provides individual tools for common text, data, and format conversions.

name: OpenStatus: Uptime and status pages
